summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted after a fall with loss of consciousness and confusion. He presented with fever, hypoglycemia, and dehydration. Initial evaluation revealed no acute intracranial abnormality, and lumbar puncture showed no evidence of central nervous system infection. His altered mental status was attributed to metabolic encephalopathy likely due to polypharmacy, alcohol use, dehydration, and uncontrolled hypertension. He was found to have a right lower extremity DVT, multiple right-sided pulmonary emboli, and a left lower lobe pneumonia, for which he was treated with anticoagulation and antibiotics. His Revlimid was held due to cytopenias, and a bone marrow biopsy was performed with results pending. His medications were simplified, and he improved clinically. He was discharged home on Arixtra, levofloxacin, labetalol, amlodipine, and thiamine, with follow-up arranged for oncology, psychiatry, and primary care.
